main.title: Ethernet: a network proposed at Xerox PARC
main.summary: Robert Metcalfe's memorandum of May 22, 1973 proposed Ethernet as a way to connect computers at Xerox PARC.

cards.heading: A local network takes shape
cards.text:
Robert Metcalfe proposed Ethernet in a memorandum at Xerox PARC on May 22, 1973. The idea provided a way for local computers to exchange data, laying the foundation for a family of wired networking standards. Ethernet reached commercial use in 1980 and was standardised in 1983.

Early versions shared coaxial cable between connected machines. Later systems adopted twisted-pair and fibre-optic links with switches, supporting more devices, longer distances and higher data rates while retaining substantial backward compatibility.

main.title: The Dark Side of the Moon
main.summary: Pink Floyd released The Dark Side of the Moon in March 1973 after developing its material through live performance.

cards.heading: The Dark Side of the Moon
cards.text: Pink Floyd released The Dark Side of the Moon in March 1973 after developing its material through live performance. The album connected pressures in the band's life with broader concerns about mental strain, including the experience of former member Syd Barrett. Recording at EMI Studios brought multitrack production, tape loops and analogue synthesisers into its carefully joined sequence. Engineer Alan Parsons shaped many details and recruited Clare Torry for The Great Gig in the Sky. The result concentrated ideas from the group's earlier experiments into an album whose sounds and transitions carry its themes together.

main.title: The Exorcist
main.summary: The Exorcist is a 1973 American supernatural horror film directed by William Friedkin and produced by William Peter Blatty, who adapted his own 1971 novel.

cards.heading: The Exorcist
cards.text:
The Exorcist is a 1973 American supernatural horror film directed by William Friedkin and produced by William Peter Blatty, who adapted his own 1971 novel. The film stars Ellen Burstyn, Max von Sydow, Jason Miller, and Linda Blair, and follows the demonic possession of a young girl and the attempt to rescue her through an exorcism by two Catholic priests.

Blatty and Friedkin had difficulty casting the film. Their choice of relative unknowns Burstyn, Blair, and Miller, instead of major stars, drew opposition from executives at Warner Bros. Principal photography was also difficult. Many cast and crew were injured, some died, and unusual accidents delayed shooting. Production took twice as long as scheduled and cost almost three times the initial budget; the many mishaps have led to a belief that the film was cursed.

main.title: Xerox Alto
main.summary: The first Xerox Alto machines appeared at Xerox PARC in March 1973.

cards.heading: Xerox Alto
cards.text: The first Xerox Alto machines appeared at Xerox PARC in March 1973. A mouse, bitmap screen and graphical interface offered ways to work with information beyond typed commands. Its text editor showed a page in a form resembling the eventual output, while Ethernet connected machines and supported shared resources. The Alto remained expensive and was produced in limited numbers, but its design influenced later personal computing. A relatively small workstation became a place to explore how documents, applications and networks might fit together in everyday use.

main.title: Autobahn
main.summary: Kraftwerk released Autobahn in November 1974, completing a move from experimental krautrock towards songs built largely from synthesisers and drum machines.

cards.heading: Autobahn
cards.text: Kraftwerk released Autobahn in November 1974, completing a move from experimental krautrock towards songs built largely from synthesisers and drum machines. Its 22-minute title track turns the pleasure of driving on German motorways into a musical journey, including sounds that suggest the vehicle itself. Florian Schneider and Ralf Hütter worked with Klaus Röder and Wolfgang Flür, recording mainly at Conny Plank's studio. Lyrics and a new visual identity developed with Emil Schult accompanied the change. The road became both the subject of the record and a way to organise its electronic sound.

main.title: Altair 8800
main.summary: The Altair 8800 reached a wide audience on the cover of Popular Electronics in January 1975.

cards.heading: Altair 8800
cards.text: The Altair 8800 reached a wide audience on the cover of Popular Electronics in January 1975. MITS sold the Intel 8080-based microcomputer by mail order to hobbyists eager to assemble and use their own machine. Its front-panel switches allowed direct programming; a serial interface and external terminal provided another way to interact with it. Interest grew quickly, helping turn microcomputing into a commercial market. The machine's expansion bus became the S-100 standard, while Altair BASIC became Microsoft's founding product. A computer kit thus helped create a wider business around compatible hardware and software.

main.title: Dolby Stereo reaches cinemas
main.summary: Lisztomania introduced a Dolby Stereo optical soundtrack to cinema audiences in 1975.

cards.heading: A wider sound from the film strip
cards.text:
Dolby Stereo reached commercial cinema in 1975 with Lisztomania, Ken Russell's film about Franz Liszt. Its optical soundtrack brought Dolby's stereo system to 35mm projection. The format developed further with full left, centre, right and surround encoding in A Star Is Born in 1976.

The Dolby Stereo name also covered noise reduction for six-channel magnetic soundtracks on 70mm film. Related technology moved into homes with Dolby Surround in 1982 and improved decoding through Dolby Pro Logic in 1987.

main.title: Homebrew Computer Club
main.summary: The Homebrew Computer Club was an early computer hobbyist group in Menlo Park, California, which met from March 1975 to December 1986.

cards.heading: Homebrew Computer Club
cards.text:
The Homebrew Computer Club was an early computer hobbyist group in Menlo Park, California, which met from March 1975 to December 1986. The club had an influential role in the development of the microcomputer revolution and the rise of that aspect of the Silicon Valley information technology industrial complex.

Several high-profile hackers and computer entrepreneurs emerged from its ranks, including Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak, the founders of Apple Computer. With its newsletter and monthly meetings promoting an open exchange of ideas, the club has been described as "the crucible for an entire industry" as it pertains to personal computing.

main.title: Jaws
main.summary: Steven Spielberg's Jaws reached cinemas in 1975, following a police chief, a marine biologist and a shark hunter trying to stop attacks on a seaside town.

cards.heading: Jaws
cards.text: Steven Spielberg's Jaws reached cinemas in 1975, following a police chief, a marine biologist and a shark hunter trying to stop attacks on a seaside town. Adapted from Peter Benchley's novel, it makes the water around an ordinary holiday destination a source of danger. Filming at sea near Martha's Vineyard proved difficult, and the mechanical sharks repeatedly malfunctioned. Spielberg often kept the animal out of sight instead. John Williams's spare, ominous theme made its approaching presence audible, allowing sound and anticipation to carry scenes before the shark appeared.

main.title: Microsoft is founded
main.summary: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft in 1975 to market BASIC interpreters for the Altair 8800.

cards.heading: Microsoft is founded
cards.text:
Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft in 1975 to market BASIC interpreters for the Altair 8800. The company later became a dominant supplier of personal-computer operating systems through MS-DOS in the mid-1980s and then Windows. Its software business expanded into internet services, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and video games.

Microsoft's 1986 public offering and the subsequent rise in its share price created considerable wealth among its employees. Under Steve Ballmer, who succeeded Gates as chief executive in 2000, the company acquired Skype in 2011, introduced its Surface computer line in 2012 and formed Microsoft Mobile through Nokia.
